concepts.name: Commander's Intent
concepts.description: A concise statement of the desired end state that guides decentralized decision making in uncertain environments.

concepts.name: Finding the Core
concepts.description: Reducing an idea to its single most important message so that people can understand, remember, and act on it.

problems.name: Plans fail in unpredictable environments
problems.description: Detailed instructions become ineffective when circumstances change and unexpected events occur.

problems.name: Too many competing priorities
problems.description: Organizations struggle to align decisions when multiple goals compete for attention.

insights.author: Chip Heath & Dan Heath
insights.chunk_file: outputs/chunks/Made to Stick - Chip and Dan Heath/chunk_009.txt
insights.title: Use intent instead of detailed plans
insights.what_it_says: In complex and unpredictable situations, detailed plans quickly become obsolete. A clear statement of intent allows people to adapt while remaining aligned with the desired outcome.
insights.why_it_matters: Teams can respond to changing conditions without waiting for new instructions.

examples_from_source.what_happened: Army leaders replaced rigid plans with concise statements describing the desired end state.
examples_from_source.why_it_matters: Soldiers could improvise when circumstances changed.
examples_from_source.transferable_lesson: Communicate outcomes rather than prescribing every action.

decision_rules.rule: State the desired outcome rather than every step.
decision_rules.action: Communicate intent and allow local adaptation.
decision_rules.rationale: Unexpected events will invalidate detailed plans.

application_patterns.adaptation_notes: Works in business, education, product development, and military operations.

tradeoffs: Less control over specific actions in exchange for greater adaptability.
insights.evidence: You can lose the ability to execute the original plan, but you never lose the responsibility of executing the intent.

insights.author: Chip Heath & Dan Heath
insights.chunk_file: outputs/chunks/Made to Stick - Chip and Dan Heath/chunk_009.txt
insights.title: Simplicity comes from identifying the core
insights.what_it_says: Making ideas stick requires identifying the single most important idea and removing competing messages.
insights.why_it_matters: People remember and act on focused ideas more effectively.

examples_from_source.example_name: Commander's Intent as a single objective
examples_from_source.what_happened: Military leaders identify one overriding objective.
examples_from_source.why_it_matters: Everyone can align around the same goal.

decision_rules.action: Remove secondary messages that compete with the main point.
decision_rules.rationale: People cannot focus on several 'most important' ideas simultaneously.

patterns.description: Reduce information until only the essential idea remains.

warnings.warning: Too many priorities dilute the message.
warnings.consequence: People struggle to remember or act.

when_not_to_use: When detailed technical reference material is required
tradeoffs: Some nuance is sacrificed for clarity.
insights.evidence: You can't have five most important goals.

relationships.evidence: inventing a concept called Commander's Intent
Finding the core means stripping an idea down to its most critical essence
